I will keep my land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and keep my machinery and labor schedule efficient. I am 62, so I value a system I know well, but because I am well educated, I would still run it in a more measured way: improved winter wheat seed for stability and disease resistance, and hybrid summer maize for stronger yield potential. I would not spread land across too many crops, because that adds management complexity, weakens scale efficiency, and raises marketing and pest-control risk. My main management choice is to stay disciplined on fertilizer, irrigation, and timing rather than chase novelty. For wheat, I would focus on steady nutrition, three irrigations around key growth stages, and two pesticide sprays if field pressure justifies them. For maize, I would push yield with hybrid seed, moderate but sufficient fertilizer, two irrigations if rainfall is not enough, and two pesticide applications centered on early pest pressure and late disease control. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage ahead of wheat to prepare a uniform seedbed, and no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and conserve moisture.
